endorsements.quote: Datasheets 12 can also be used for transparency of the data sources, and to clarify use-cases that might require more care.
Ensure that the training sample is representative of the population the AI/ML model is intended for and carefully examine inclusion and exclusion criteria.

It is important to note that if you are using a benchmark dataset for the selection of a model among multiple candidates, you should consequently use an independent evaluation dataset to evaluate the performance of the selected model in an unbiased manner.

Best annotation practices should include multiple annotators, intra- and interannotator comparisons; annotator pools should be inclusive, diverse, multi-institutional, and—depending on the desired endpoint—include annotators with different levels of experience.

Similarly, collaboration with social researchers and other subject matter experts may contribute to minimize historical bias by understanding and correcting for how historical factors may shape data distributions for specific groups and by understanding and correcting for how a “tainted” reference standard and external factors may affect data and algorithmic performance.
It can be measured by evaluating the trained AI/ML model on different subpopulations or by training it with data with different prevalence.

unlisted_practices: Use globally unique identifiers (GUIDs) to trace data sources and avoid duplicate use of the same cases across aggregated public datasets.
Split training, validation, and test sets at the patient level so all data from one patient stay in a single set.
Evaluate whether synthetic data mitigate bias for each task without introducing new biases before using them.
Account for correlated observations (e.g., multiple lesions per patient) when estimating performance and variance.
Use annotators independent of those for the training data to establish the reference standard for performance testing.
Provide well-defined annotation guidance and standardized lexicons, and share them with investigators who use the data.
Consult human-computer interface experts and carefully design user interfaces and presentation order to minimize presentation bias in annotation and reader studies.
Use the highest available level of reference standard that correlates with patient outcomes for training and testing.
Do not rely on excluding protected characteristics to mitigate historical bias, since AI can infer withheld attributes.
Systematically monitor and continually evaluate model usage after deployment to detect mismatches between intended and actual use.
Retrain and reassess models with more recent data to address concept drift.

screen.reason: This is a framework/recommendations paper developed by a multi-institutional expert panel outlining 29 potential sources of bias across the AI lifecycle in medical imaging and proposing mitigation strategies and best practices.
